source_construct: L31: async with async_session() as session (FastAPI yield dependency)
target_translation: One *database.Session per HTTP request, opened by an explicit call at the top of each handler that uses it (RULEBOOK §2: get_db_session becomes an explicit call) with 'defer session.Close()'. The handler commits where the Python handler commits (commits are in admin.py, boxes.py, indieauth.py, webmentions.py, incoming_activities.py:46, uploads.py:100 and httpsig.py:148; the POST /inbox handler writes through new_ap_incoming_activity (main.py:1173) and the httpsig check can update an actor and commit in the request's session, so those paths are not read-only). A request that ends without commit loses its changes: Close() rolls back. The error path: the Python session is closed and rolled back BEFORE an HTTPException handler runs (see the custom_http_exception_handler row), so with a Go defer, the wrapper must write the error page after the handler function returns. No stale-object effect inside one request beyond the identity-map rules of RULEBOOK §2 (expire_on_commit=False keeps old values after a commit; the Go structs do too). Connection setup keeps the 15 s busy timeout.
evidence: database.py:24 (expire_on_commit=False, autoflush default True), :22 (timeout 15), :30-35 (yield, then close in finally); fastapi 0.78 middleware order: fastapi/applications.py:161-188 (AsyncExitStackMiddleware is inside ExceptionMiddleware, so the teardown runs when the exception leaves the router); fastapi/middleware/asyncexitstack.py:15-29; ADR 0017 (Session, rollback on close); commits in the request session: incoming_activities.py:46 (called from main.py:1173), httpsig.py:147-148, uploads.py:100

source_construct: L237: async with async_session() as db_session (error page for text/html)
target_translation: A second, short session that the error-page code opens for itself, only when the Accept header starts with 'text/html' and 400 <= status < 600 (otherwise return the JSON error with no session). Read-only: render error.html through render_template, then Close() (rolls back; nothing is committed). Title: 404 'Oops, nothing to see here', 500 'Oops, something went wrong', else the error's detail. The request's own session is already closed by then, so uncommitted changes of the failed request are gone; do not reuse it.
evidence: main.py:226-254; fastapi/applications.py:161-188 and fastapi/middleware/asyncexitstack.py:15-29 (dependency teardown runs before ExceptionMiddleware calls the handler); render_template only reads (templates.py:83+); the 'finally: close()' at main.py:252-253 duplicates the context manager's close

source_construct: L118: async with async_session() as db_session (CLI prune)
target_translation: One session for the whole command. prune_old_data runs three DELETEs (incoming activities, outgoing activities, inbox objects), then Commit() once (prune.py:30), then 'VACUUM'. VACUUM must run OUTSIDE a transaction (SQLite refuses it inside one), so the Go Session needs a statement that runs on the connection without BEGIN after the commit; a normal session.Exec that autobegins would fail. An error before the commit rolls all three DELETEs back when the session closes. The deletes use synchronize_session=False: no ORM objects are kept, nothing stale.
evidence: prune.py:20-32 (commit at :30, VACUUM at :32 after it), :116-119; execution_options(synchronize_session=False) at :46, :62, :111; ADR 0017 (Session begins a transaction at its first statement)

source_construct: L124: async with async_session() as db_session (read-only stats)

No commit; Close() ends it. The rows are used AFTER the session closes (printing row.anybox_object.ap_id and the other columns), so the Go code must load both related objects inside the session, because there is no lazy load afterwards.

source_construct: L284: async with async_session() as db_session (move_to task)
target_translation: One session for one task run. Resolve the account first (webfinger; get_actor_url errors print 'ERROR: Failed to resolve ...' with a trace and return), fetch_actor (it may Insert a new actor row, which is not committed), check LOCAL_ACTOR.ap_id in alsoKnownAs, then send_move, which commits at boxes.py:554. Every early return (resolve failure, missing alsoKnownAs) leaves without a commit, so Close() rolls back the actor row that fetch_actor flushed: keep that (do not commit on the early paths). Print 'Done' after the session closes. The error text printed at tasks.py:289-290 is the Python traceback: ADR 0023 covers only the four worker sites that store an activity's error column, so it does not allow a different printed text here. TODO(port): keep the printed text or get an ADR (an owner question). Note: the message at tasks.py:293 is not an f-string and prints the literal '{moved_to}': BUG(port) keep the text.
evidence: tasks.py:282-309 (returns at :290, :294, :303 inside the with-block); fetch_actor flushes only, actor.py:226, :307 (no commit in actor.py); send_move boxes.py:529-554 (commit at :554); ADR 0017 (close without commit rolls back); docs/adr/0023-store-go-error-text-instead-of-tracebacks.md (only the worker error columns), printed trace at tasks.py:289-290

source_construct: L402: async with async_session() as db_session (import task)
target_translation: One session for the whole import, with ONE Commit after the loop (tasks.py:419). Reads _get_following once (the set of followed actor ids, with the actor joined), then for each (handle, actor_url) from the CSV: skip if already in the set, else _send_follow (fetch_actor, save outbox Follow, new outgoing activity; none of them commits) and count++. The set is not updated inside the loop, so a repeated actor_url in the CSV sends two follows: keep that. An error in the loop propagates out, the session closes without commit and every follow of this run is rolled back (including the already-counted ones): keep that. The CSV lookups (webfinger over the network) run inside the session before the loop: get_actor_urls... is awaited once, at tasks.py:409, before any follow is written. Go note: the first read begins a transaction in the Go Session, which may then hold an old WAL snapshot during the network calls (ADR 0017 decides the Session's begin).
evidence: tasks.py:400-421; _send_follow boxes.py:339-359 ('Caller should commit'); _get_following boxes.py:953-962; get_actor_urls_from_following_accounts_csv_file utils/mastodon.py:14-30
